gaps.sentence: He's been ___ from work since his operation.
gaps.explanation: 'Be away from work / off work' are natural; 'absent from work' is formal but fits the gap 'from work' already present? The gap is '___ from work' — 'away' fits.

gaps.sentence: She's ___ of winning a medal this season.
gaps.explanation: 'Be capable of doing' = have the ability/skill; 'able' needs 'able to do'.

gaps.sentence: They walked ___ the tunnel to reach the other side.
gaps.hint: inside and out the other side
gaps.explanation: 'Through' = in one side and out the other (3-D); 'across' = from side to side on a surface.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget ___ my first tournament.
gaps.explanation: 'Forget + -ing' = fail to recall a past event; 'forget to do' = fail to do a duty.

gaps.sentence: The play was a complete ___ — nobody came.
The meal was absolutely ___ — my compliments to the chef.
gaps.explanation: 'Delicious' = very tasty. 'Delighted' describes people who are pleased.

gaps.sentence: It ___ me ten minutes to realise my mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'It took me ten minutes to do…'; 'spend' needs 'I spent ten minutes doing'.

gaps.sentence: Her speech ___ everyone in the audience.
gaps.explanation: A verb is needed: impressed. 'Impressive' is an adjective.
